page_title: Realtime Django Part 4: Build a Chat application with django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js (Plug the Vue frontend into the django API)

summary.title: Realtime Django Part 4: Build a Chat application with django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js (Plug the Vue frontend into the django API)
summary.one_liner: Learn how to wire a Vue.js chat UI to a Django REST API, covering start/join sessions, sending messages, and polling for new messages, and why WebSockets are more efficient.
keywords: connect vue to django rest api
why use websockets instead of polling
takeaways: Use a Vue component with a sessionStarted flag to switch between the start-chat view and the chat window.
Match optional URL parameters with Vue Router (e.g. /chats/:uri?) and read them via this.$route.params.
Start sessions with a POST to the DRF API, join sessions with a PATCH, and store messages in component data rendered with v-if.
Polling with setInterval gives the illusion of realtime but multiplies requests and wastes bandwidth as users grow.
WebSockets provide a persistent two-way connection so the server can push new messages; the next part integrates them via uWSGI.
summary.summary: The article is Part 4 of a series building a realtime chat app with Django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js. It walks through designing a Start/Join chat component, using Vue Router with optional parameters to capture the chat URI, and calling the Part 3 DRF API to create sessions, join with PATCH, and send and display messages. It then adds automatic updates via setInterval polling every 3 seconds, works through the request-count cost of polling, and introduces WebSockets as the more efficient alternative to be covered in the next part.
